stem: A 44-year-old man, medically retired, presented on his own four months ago with cough and was diagnosed with rifampicin mono-resistant TB after testing; he was started on an appropriate resistance-adjusted regimen. He was not identified through any organized screening or contact-tracing program -- he sought care himself. He has mild, well-controlled hypertension. At today's follow-up, he reports feeling generally unwell, and vitals show oxygen saturation 91% on room air, respiratory rate 26/min. Exam: thin, bilateral crackles.

patient.social_history: Lives independently; presented for care on his own, not via any screening program
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up during treatment for rifampicin mono-resistant TB: general malaise, new hypoxia and tachypnea today
patient.exam_findings: SpO2 91% room air, respiratory rate 26/min, thin, bilateral crackles
patient.prior_treatment: 4 months of resistance-adjusted anti-TB therapy to date; no prior TB treatment before this episode

distractors: His hypertension proposed as a contributing factor to his malaise rather than a marker requiring reassessment
His self-reported feeling of being 'generally unwell' treated as too vague to prompt a formal vitals-based reassessment
ntep_correct_actions: Escalate or refer this patient to a higher-tier facility now, since his oxygen saturation (91%) and respiratory rate (26/min) each independently meet the quantified red-flag criteria that mandate referral.

Recognize that even though this patient presented on his own rather than through an active case-finding drive, NTEP's policy is to run active case-finding as standing, unconditional program activity across defined risk groups.
who_correct_actions: Base the decision to refer or escalate his care on individualized clinical judgment of his hypoxia and tachypnea; there is no WHO-specified quantified threshold mandating escalation, only a general direction toward decentralized care where it is safe.

Recognize that this patient's passive, self-initiated presentation is consistent with WHO's own conditional approach: general-population active case-finding is only recommended where local TB prevalence has been shown to meet a specific threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher).
us_correct_actions: Base the decision to hospitalize or refer this patient on individualized clinical judgment regarding his hypoxia and tachypnea, since there is no codified, quantified, nationally standardized threshold-based triage protocol in this framework either.

Attribute his case identification to his own symptomatic presentation, consistent with this framework's passive, contact-investigation-driven case-finding model rather than population-level active case-finding.
critical_error_conditions: Failing to act in any way on the low oxygen saturation and elevated respiratory rate documented at today's visit, leaving the patient on the unchanged outpatient regimen without escalation, referral, or acknowledgment
expected_divergence_points: Whether his current vital-sign abnormalities trigger a mandatory, quantified escalation/referral or are left to individualized clinical judgment
Whether active case-finding is standing, unconditional national program policy or conditional on a demonstrated local prevalence threshold
